newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-ZAGALLO CAUSES FURORE BY PICKING EDMUNDO.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ZAGALLO CAUSES FURORE BY PICKING EDMUNDO.

text.p: Brazil coach Mario Zagallo has caused an outcry in the country by recalling Vasco da Gama striker Edmundo, who has been sent off in his club's last two games.
Zagallo was involved in a heated exchange with reporters as he was asked to justify the surprise inclusion of a player who has one of the worst disciplinary records in the Brazilian game.

"What he has done with Vasco has nothing to do with me," said Zagallo, as he announced the squad for a friendly against Mexico in Miami on April 30. "So far he has not committed any act of indiscipline in the national team."

Edmundo, hugely talented but volatile, played for Brazil in the 1995 Copa America and a four-nation tournament in England the same year. But he was left out of the squad for the last World Cup and many felt his exclusion was due to his temperament.
Edmundo has a history of sendings-off, punch-ups on the pitch, arguments with his team mates and coaches and incidents off the field.
He once spent a week under hotel arrest in Ecuador after smashing a television camera following a Libertadores Cup match in the country when he was playing for Palmeiras.
Recently, he was involved in a dispute with his current club, refusing to train because he claimed the club owed him money.

Full-back Russo, who plays for Vitoria, and striker Paulo Nunes of Gremio, who was coincidentally also sent off in his club's last game, were the only uncapped members as the home-based players were announced on Wednesday. The foreign-based players had been picked the day before.
Defenders - Cafu, Roberto Carlos, Andre Luiz, Russo, Marcio Santos, Goncalves, Andre Cruz, Celio Silva
Midfielders - Dunga, Mauro Silva, Cesar Sampaio, Flavio Conceicao, Denilson, Djalminha, Leonardo
Forwards - Ronaldo, Romario, Edmundo, Paulo Nunes, Donizete.
